rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 3 "Where the four task sizes come from", line 23: "Same sizes as the prework, now sourced from the game's own backlog:" — "the prework" is a cross-file noun never named earlier in this file, but this exact phrase is the compendium's own worked PASS example under §2's navigational-pointer carve-out ("'the prework' passes"), and this file is reachable only via a link inside prework.md §1 per its own Meta note, so the referent is the reader's immediate prior context. Second-closest: chunk 2, line 19, "...material you'll want when the later tasks need it" — "the later tasks" is a forward reference never concretely named in this file up to this point, but it stays inside: it is generic reading-order framing ("you'll need this eventually"), not a claim requiring a specific antecedent, and no reader-comprehension harm follows from leaving it unresolved. All other referents (the game, the page, the .html, the repo, the data feature you seeded, the running game/test suite/commit history/the one bug) resolve against the same or an earlier chunk of this file.

Only cross-file mention in body: chunk 3, line 23, "the prework" — named, not located, matching the carve-out's own canonical PASS example verbatim. No file is pointed at by position ("the opening lecture said", "earlier document").

All 5 chunks (incl. chunk 0) carry a self-standing claim or a concrete bulleted list; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 4 ("## Bring to Module 1") is a one-sentence checklist naming four concrete artifacts already established earlier in the file, which is a self-carrying Bring-to-Module close, not an orphan.

Checked each header against its chunk's content, header covered then uncovered: "Get to a running game" -> chunk delivers the build steps that reach a running game; "Leave it with tests and a data surface" -> chunk adds tests, commits, and a data-touching feature; "Where the four task sizes come from" -> chunk sources the four sizes from the game's backlog; "Bring to Module 1" -> chunk lists exactly what to bring. No header is contradicted by its body.

Closest call is the anaphora sub-item: chunk 2's three bullets (lines 17-19) all open "Ask Claude to [add/commit/add]..." — a genuine triple — but the third leg ("add one feature that touches data or other players: a shareable level via a URL, a score you submit, or saved progress") carries substantially more new concrete content than the first two, which is the rule's own stated escape ("third leg carries NEW concrete content"), so it stays inside. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction anywhere. No self-grading superlative (no "one of the most/best" framing). No number-with-own-retraction (line 12's "two levels, and three lemming actions" is a plain instruction, not a hedged measurement). No abstraction-noun-stack coinage ("surface area" line 12 and "a data surface" header line 15 are plain engineering terms, not compressed abstractions like "the bounded-window reality"). No verb triplet with an empty leg.
